McKinsey & Company surveyed 419 B2B pricing executives and asked two questions.
 
(1) Where is your biggest margin opportunity? 62% named discount approval and governance.
 
(2) Where are you putting the money? 22% named discount approval and governance.
 
Renewals scored worse: 60% for impact. 13% for investment.

Etched went from $10.3B to $21B in 26 days.

The obvious lesson is about AI infrastructure.

The more useful lesson is about sequencing.

Etched did not suddenly become valuable because it announced another funding round.

Before the latest repricing, several things had happened:

Its chip had been manufactured successfully.

The company said it had more than $1B in customer contracts.

It raised $300M at a $10.3B valuation in July.

Then Jane Street tested the hardware, became the first customer, and deployed a rack.

A few weeks later, investors priced the company at $21B.

The order matters.

A lot of founders try to raise conviction with bigger claims.
